title: src/types.ts is fully unused — duplicates types defined in manifest.ts
description: src/types.ts defines PoolDescriptor, ManifestPoolEntry, DeploymentManifest, and LoadedManifest, but no source or test file imports anything from this module. Grep across src/ and tests/ for `from.*types` returns zero matches. The two types actually used at runtime (PoolDescriptor and LoadedManifest) are re-declared inside src/manifest.ts, and every consumer (App.tsx, dataLayer.ts, manifest.test.ts) imports them from './manifest.js'.
impact: Dead module that will mislead future maintainers — they will edit one definition, the runtime will silently keep using the other. Also defeats the AC1.6 audit signal: the doc-comment that cites notes/chain-shape.md as the derivation source lives in the file nobody reads, while the live duplicate in manifest.ts has no such citation.
recommendation: Delete src/types.ts entirely OR delete the duplicate type declarations from src/manifest.ts and have manifest.ts re-export from types.ts. Pick one home for these types and ensure all imports converge there.

title: computeMarketStats / aggregateFills / fetchFills are wired only to tests, not to the running app
description: runDataLayer issues sui_getObject and suix_queryEvents calls but discards every response: it returns Promise<void>, never invokes computeMarketStats, aggregateFills, or fetchFills, and never feeds anything into PoolCardData. main.tsx's fetchPoolStats stub returns hard-coded zeros and undefineds. The compute pipeline (marketStats.ts, fillAggregator.ts, fillFetcher.ts — ~230 LOC) is therefore reachable only from its unit tests and is dead code from the runtime's perspective.
impact: The dev-server boot specified by AC1.1 will mount and render six PoolCards full of sentinels, regardless of chain state. Reviewers reading the source will assume the green tests prove the full pipeline works end-to-end; in fact the connecting glue is missing. This is the largest accidental-complexity-vs-actual-behavior gap in the cycle.
recommendation: Either (a) wire dataLayer.ts to call computeMarketStats and aggregateFills against the parsed RPC payloads, return PoolCardData[], and have main.tsx use it; or (b) shrink the tests-only modules to whatever the runtime actually needs and document the deferred wiring as out-of-scope for this cycle. Right now it is a tautology farm: the tests pass but exercise nothing the user sees.

title: main.tsx contains `void loadManifest; void RPC_URL;` — dead-import suppression
description: main.tsx imports loadManifest and defines RPC_URL but never uses either. The `void loadManifest; void RPC_URL;` lines are present solely to silence unused-symbol warnings. The actual deps.loadManifest is an inline reimplementation that fetches '/localnet.json' and re-parses the same JSON shape that loadManifest already handles.
impact: Two parallel manifest loaders exist (loadManifest in manifest.ts uses node:fs; the inline one in main.tsx uses fetch), each with its own validation logic and error messages. They will drift. The `void` statements are a code smell that signals 'the right thing should be wired here but isn't yet'.
recommendation: Either remove the unused loadManifest import and RPC_URL constant outright, or refactor loadManifest to accept an injectable reader (fs vs fetch) and reuse it from main.tsx. Drop the `void X` placeholders.

title: PoolDescriptor / LoadedManifest interface declared in three places
description: PoolDescriptor and LoadedManifest are declared in src/types.ts (lines 10-15, 29-32) AND src/manifest.ts (lines 14-19, 21-24). PoolCard's SparklinePoint shape is also re-declared in src/components/PoolCard.tsx (lines 11-14) instead of being imported from src/fillAggregator.ts where the same shape exists (lines 16-19). Three near-duplicate sources of truth for shapes the spec wants derived from chain-shape.md.
impact: When chain-shape evolves, the maintainer has to find and update N copies. The risk is silent drift between the type the test asserts on and the type the runtime actually receives.
recommendation: Promote types.ts to the canonical home; export PoolDescriptor, LoadedManifest, FillRecord, SparklinePoint, MarketStats from there and import everywhere else. Delete the duplicate declarations.

title: RunDataLayerArgs duplicates manifest typing inline instead of importing LoadedManifest
description: RunDataLayerArgs.manifest is typed inline as `{ network?: ...; packages?: { deepbook?: { packageId?: string } }; pools?: Record<string, { poolId: string; baseCoinType: string; quoteCoinType: string }> }`, which is a slightly weaker version of DeploymentManifest already declared in types.ts and a slightly different version of what manifest.loadManifest returns (LoadedManifest). The same inline shape appears again in main.tsx's loadManifest stub.
impact: Three subtly different views of the same JSON structure live across the codebase. Each accepts inputs the others would reject (e.g. main.tsx tolerates missing packages.deepbook entirely; dataLayer treats it as optional then defaults to ''; manifest.loadManifest throws).
recommendation: Type the manifest argument as `DeploymentManifest` (raw JSON shape) or `LoadedManifest` (validated) — pick one, define it once, import everywhere.

title: rpcId is a module-level mutable counter — needless global state
description: `let rpcId = 0;` at module scope is incremented inside rpc(). JSON-RPC ids only need to be unique within a single client/connection lifetime (and most servers do not care). A monotonically increasing global counter is the kind of state that hurts test isolation (the value leaks across tests in the same process) and adds zero behavioral value.
impact: Tiny — but it's the kind of premature 'production-flavored' detail the contract explicitly excludes (Out of scope: production-grade caching, retry/backoff). Module-level mutable state in an otherwise pure functional module reads as accidental complexity.
recommendation: Use Date.now() or a local counter inside runDataLayer, or simply pass `id: 1` — the responses are processed sequentially and id correlation is not used.

title: PoolCard's fmt() guards against `null` after a TypeScript-narrowed `number | undefined`
description: fmt(value: number | undefined) checks `value === undefined || value === null || !Number.isFinite(value)`. The `=== null` branch is unreachable: the parameter type is `number | undefined`, so TypeScript guarantees value is never null. Defensive code that the type system already covers adds noise and suggests the author didn't trust the types.
impact: Cosmetic. A reader pauses to wonder when null could appear and concludes 'never'.
recommendation: Drop the `value === null` check, or widen the parameter type to `number | null | undefined` if the data source ever produces null.

title: main.tsx reads import.meta.env via `as unknown as` cast instead of using Vite's typed env
description: RPC_URL is computed via `(import.meta as unknown as { env?: { VITE_SUI_RPC_URL?: string } }).env?.VITE_SUI_RPC_URL ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:9000'`. Vite ships an `ImportMetaEnv` augmentation that makes `import.meta.env.VITE_SUI_RPC_URL` typed without any cast — just add a one-line `vite-env.d.ts` with `/// <reference types="vite/client" />`. The double cast (`as unknown as`) is a code smell about types in general.
impact: Cosmetic + propagation: any future env var added the same way will repeat the cast pattern.
recommendation: Add `src/vite-env.d.ts` containing `/// <reference types="vite/client" />` and reference `import.meta.env.VITE_SUI_RPC_URL` directly. Even simpler: hardcode the localnet URL since this is dev-only and the contract pins it.

title: Two parallel DAY_MS constants in fillAggregator.ts and fillFetcher.ts
description: fillAggregator.ts and fillFetcher.ts both declare `const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;` independently. Same value, same purpose (24h rolling window per AC1.5).
impact: Trivial. If the rolling window ever changes (e.g. to 12h or 48h for testing), the two will silently disagree and the test suite covers each function in isolation so the inconsistency would not be caught.
recommendation: Hoist DAY_MS into a small constants module or into types.ts and import from both places.

title: computeMarketStats one-sided depth branch duplicates the two-sided loop body
description: The depth-summing logic appears three times: once in the two-sided branch (asks loop + bids loop within ±1% of mid) and twice more in the one-sided fallback (one for asks-only anchored on bestAsk, one for bids-only anchored on bestBid). Each is a six-line `for ... if (lvl.price >= lo && lvl.price <= hi) ...` loop. A single helper `sumDepthInWindow(levels, anchor)` would collapse the three sites to three one-liners.
impact: Limited. The three loops are correct today but the duplication makes the one-sided fallback semantics (anchor on the present side's best, not on a missing mid) less obvious — a reader has to compare three loop bodies to spot what differs.
recommendation: Extract `function depthAround(anchor: number, levels: {price:number, qty:number}[]): number`. Replace the three loop bodies with single calls.

title: App's status:'loading'|'ready'|'error' state machine could be derived
description: AppState has three explicit statuses but the same information is encoded by `cards`/`error` presence: error set => error UI; cards populated => ready; otherwise loading. A single `cards: PoolCardData[] | undefined` plus `error: string | undefined` would suffice. With React 19 available the spec mentions Suspense as a more idiomatic alternative.
impact: None functionally — three-state union is fine and arguably clearer. Flagging as info because the contract sized this cycle at ~200-300 LOC and ended at ~600; minor state-modeling savings here would chip away at that.
recommendation: Optional: collapse to derived state, or leave as-is. Either is defensible. The bigger LOC sink is dead modules (R4-001, R4-002), not this state shape.

title: Cycle deliverable is ~600 LOC vs spec envelope of 200-300 LOC TS
description: Total src LOC across the nine TS/TSX files is 603 (wc -l). The contract's stack pins section and the simplicity envelope referenced for this cycle anticipated ~200-300 LOC for a single-route React + Vite shell. Roughly half of the excess is justified by the chain-shape complexity (u128 order-id decoding alone is real work). The other half is duplication and dead-wiring identified in R4-001, R4-002, R4-003, R4-004.
impact: If R4-001/002/003/004 are addressed (delete types.ts, wire dataLayer to compute, drop main.tsx voids, dedupe shared types), the deliverable shrinks toward the envelope without losing behavior.
recommendation: Use the consolidated review to decide whether the LOC overshoot is bought-and-paid-for (chain-shape correctness) or accidental (the duplications above). My read is ~70/30 in favor of accidental.
